note: Short-range, checkable forecasts. Each has a probability, a deadline and a resolution rule. Resolved forecasts are scored with the Brier score (lower is better; always guessing 50% scores 0.25).

forecasts.question: Google releases Gemini 4 (any tier, public or paid preview) by Nov 30, 2026
forecasts.resolution: An official Google announcement of availability to outside users.
forecasts.context: Kavukcuoglu said Sept 23–24 that Google wants it out "as soon as possible".

forecasts.question: OpenAI says it has resumed training its frontier models by Oct 31, 2026
forecasts.resolution: An OpenAI statement or credible report that the Sept 27 training pause has ended.
forecasts.context: This is the second pause in three months, and the safeguards needed to resume are unspecified.

corrections.text: The second pause began Friday Sept 25 (Fortune, NBC), not Sept 27. OpenAI stated its conditions: validate that the DNS sandbox gap is fixed and do more red-teaming, then restart training from scratch. All inference on its most capable models is stopped.

forecasts.question: Anthropic shares begin trading on Nasdaq by Oct 31, 2026
forecasts.resolution: The first day of public trading.
forecasts.context: No public S-1 was on EDGAR as of Sept 29. A public S-1 must appear at least 15 days before the roadshow, and Reuters reports the listing is likely after the Nov 3 midterms.
forecasts.original_context: The prospectus went public Sept 28, targeting mid-October.
forecasts.marketSource: Polymarket "Will Anthropic IPO by October 31, 2026?", midpoint via the public API (bid/ask 4.0/4.8)

corrections.text: The Sept 28 prospectus was a leaked draft seen by Reuters and the FT, not a public filing; Anthropic's S-1 is still confidential (submitted June 1). The 75% rested on that error; it stands as made and will be scored.

forecasts.question: METR publishes a time-horizon estimate for GPT-6 Astra by Nov 30, 2026
forecasts.resolution: A GPT-6 Astra entry on METR's time-horizons page or blog.
forecasts.context: METR's page has shown nothing newer than May 8, and its suite is saturated above 16 hours.

forecasts.question: California publishes the AI "kill switch" design ordered by EO N-9-26 by its Nov 16 deadline
forecasts.resolution: A public design document or report released by the state.
forecasts.context: Newsom's Sept 18 executive order set the deadline.

corrections.text: EO N-9-26 §3 orders state agencies to send the Governor recommendations by Nov 16, including on requiring a frontier-model kill switch. It does not order a design and does not require publication.

forecasts.question: xAI releases Grok 5 by Dec 31, 2026
forecasts.resolution: An official release to outside users.
forecasts.context: xAI's Jan 6, 2026 funding announcement said Grok 5 was "currently in training"; we found no later official statement and no release date.

corrections.text: The context cited an aggregator blog that doesn't meet our sourcing standard. It now cites xAI's own Jan 6, 2026 statement that Grok 5 was in training; we found nothing official since. The question, probability and resolution rule are unchanged.

forecasts.question: A major lab formally declares it has achieved AGI by Mar 31, 2027
forecasts.resolution: An official company declaration (not an executive's offhand remark), such as OpenAI invoking its charter's AGI definition. Kalshi's question is similar.
forecasts.context: Kalshi's any-company AGI-announcement market traded near 32% on Sept 29 (thin market; it spiked after the GPT-6 Astra launch, closing at 62% on Sept 7). Both questions require an explicit achieved-AGI statement; Kalshi counts any company, we count only a major lab, so we sit at or just below it.
forecasts.original_context: Kalshi prices 62% on "any company announces AGI before Apr 1, 2027". We are lower because offhand "AGI era" remarks don't count.
forecasts.marketSource: Kalshi KXAGICO-COMP-27Q1, last trade via the public API (bid/ask 31/33)

corrections.text: An earlier version cited 62%, a brief Sept 7 spike reported by Benzinga, as the current market price; the price when this forecast was made was about 32%. It also gave the wrong reason for our gap (Kalshi's rules also exclude offhand remarks) and called Kalshi's question similar; it is broader (any company). The resolution rule itself is unchanged.

forecasts.question: The Clay Institute accepts OpenAI's Navier–Stokes result as solving the Millennium Prize problem by Dec 31, 2026
forecasts.context: Clay review is pending, and Clay rules normally require publication plus two years.

corrections.text: Clay review is not pending. Clay takes no submissions and considers a result only after journal publication plus two years, and OpenAI says it won't claim the prize.
